fields.reasoning: internal/index/index.go already has one recovery mechanism: a rebuild that empties every table and catches up from nothing, triggered by a vanished path or a schema-version mismatch, and the package doc calls the index disposable. Keying a rebuild on the decoded FormatVersion reuses that path with one stored value and one comparison, so it cannot drift from FoldLog the way a partial re-decode of only newer-format problem rows could (re-decoding would also have to refold every touched change set and recompute both views, i.e. most of a rebuild anyway). Format bumps are rare (one per release like #424), so a full rebuild's cost is paid seldom. Rebuilding on any difference, not only a rise, also covers a downgrade then upgrade, where a lower binary stored problems for entries it could not read. It meets the intent's acceptance test: write a v(N+1) entry, open with FormatVersion N (problem stored), then N+1 (rebuilt, folds clean). The 14G of orphan dbs is a real but separate issue (cache hygiene across worktrees, not wrong folds); the intent lists it only as a side note, and widening this fix would delay unsticking landed change sets, so it is left for its own change set.
fields.statement: The persistent index stores the entry.FormatVersion it decoded with (a meta row beside the listing fingerprint) and, on Open, treats a stored version different from the binary's as stale and rebuilds from nothing, the same path a vanished file or another schema version takes; it does not selectively re-decode problem rows. Pruning index databases of worktrees that no longer exist is out of this change set's scope and is not done here; it belongs to a separate change set.
